fields.meta_title: Book Landing Page Builder With Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A book landing page turns readers into buyers. See pre-order, free-chapter, launch and author pages, then build one by prompt. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Book Landing Page With a Buy Link for Every Format
fields.hero_description: Build a book landing page with a buy link for each format, a free chapter for signups, and a reader list you own.
fields.features_heading: Everything Between the Cover and the Checkout
fields.features_subheading: The retailer takes the payment. Everything a reader sees before the buy button is the page's job.
fields.feature_1:
One buy link per format

List every format once, with hardcover, paperback, ebook, and audiobook each pointing to its retailers. Emergent builds the buttons, and the page counts the clicks on each one.
fields.feature_2:
Pre-order receipts read into fields

Readers who pre-order upload a receipt to claim the bonus. The app reads the format and order date into fields, and any receipt it cannot read clearly goes to you to check.
fields.feature_3:
A sample chapter for an email

Offer the first chapter in exchange for an email address. Every signup is saved as a row in a database you own, stamped with the date and the name of the reader who asked for it.
fields.feature_4:
Signups copied to your newsletter

Connect the email service you already use through its API, and each new reader joins your list as well as your table. Slack and HubSpot connect the same way, for alerts or a CRM.
fields.feature_5:
Release date changed in one message

Tell Emergent the new date, such as "Release moves to April 7," and it updates the pre-order banner and the countdown clock together. New review quotes go in the same way.
fields.feature_6:
The page as code in your repository

Export the finished page to your GitHub repository on paid plans, or keep it hosted on Emergent under your own domain, which uses credits. Either way, you edit it by prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Book Landing Page Examples by Goal
fields.tab_content_1:
Signed bookplates for readers who pre-order

Ines Calloway's debut novel, The Tidewater Clock, comes out March 3. Until then, her page offers a signed bookplate to anyone who uploads a pre-order receipt. Each receipt's format and order date land in the claims table, next to the reader's name. Receipts it cannot read clearly go to Ines to check.
fields.tab_content_2:
A free chapter drew 1,240 signups

Quiet Margins opens with a chapter on pricing advisory work, and Dalia Brandt gives it away for an email address. In 4 weeks the page collected 1,240 signups. Each new reader is copied to her newsletter list through its API, and her welcome email goes out from the tool she already uses.
fields.tab_content_3:
Hardcover beat ebook and audiobook in launch week

In launch week, Theo Marchetti's page for the Weeknight Pantry cookbook sent 2,000 readers to retailers. Hardcover drew 1,020 clicks, ebook 640, and audiobook 340, each counted by its own button. Theo then moved the hardcover button above the recipe preview.
fields.tab_content_4:
Visit requests from clubs of 10 or more go to Wren

Wren Halvorsen's trilogy, The Lantern Coast, sits on her author page in reading order, with a buy link under each book. Book clubs can ask for a video visit. A club of 10 or more readers goes to Wren to schedule. Smaller clubs get the discussion guide by email.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Book Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a book landing page that turns a visit into a sale or a signup, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Lead with the cover and a hook
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give every format its own button
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Trade a sample for an email
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a visitor should do first: buy the book or join your list for a sample chapter. One main action keeps the page short and the results easy to read. Put smaller asks, such as following you on social media, near the bottom.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Place the cover beside a single sentence that says what the book is and who will love it. Add the release date if the book is not out yet. On a phone, a reader should see the cover and the hook without scrolling.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List hardcover, paperback, ebook, and audiobook separately, each with links to the stores that carry it. Label each button with the format, not only the store name. A reader who listens on the commute should reach the audiobook in one tap.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the first chapter, or a short story set in the same world, behind an email field. Ask for a name and an email address and nothing more. Send the chapter right away, so the first email a reader gets from you is the one they asked for.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Quote two short blurbs from early reviews, each with the reviewer's name and where the review ran. Print only quotes you have permission to use. Below them, add a short author bio with a photo and a link to your other books.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it on your own phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the page on a phone before you share the link. Tap every buy button and confirm it opens the right format at the right store. Then sign up for the sample yourself to check that the email arrives and its link opens the chapter.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Compare clicks by format each week
fields.howto_step_7_des: After launch, set each format's clicks against the week before. If one format draws fewer clicks than you expected, move its button higher or check its price at each store. Change one thing at a time, then compare again the next week.

faq_plan.q: What is a book landing page?
faq_plan.a: A book landing page is a single web page built to sell one book or to gather readers for it. It pairs the cover with a short pitch and store links for every format. It can also offer an opening chapter to readers who leave an email address.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a book landing page?
faq_plan.a: Decide the one action you want, such as a pre-order, and gather the cover and your retailer links. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It builds the page and a table for every signup, and you change any part by prompt.

faq_plan.q: What do strong book landing page examples have in common?
faq_plan.a: They put the cover and a one-line pitch first and ask for one action. Good book landing page examples also show proof from readers, such as a short review quote, before the buy buttons. When you study a gallery, note where each page places its first button and what it asks the reader to do.

faq_plan.q: What sections does a book landing page template need?
faq_plan.a: It needs six sections: the cover and hook, buy links by format, a short description, review quotes, an author bio, and a sample-chapter signup. In a book landing page template, that last section works like a lead generation landing page, with one email field and one offer. On a page Emergent builds, each signup is saved to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What does a good book landing page example look like for a debut novel?
faq_plan.a: It leads with the cover and the release date, then a pre-order button for each format. A debut has no backlist. A book landing page example for a first novel leans on an early blurb as proof instead. A pre-order bonus, such as a signed bookplate, gives readers a reason to order before launch day.

faq_plan.q: Does each book in a series need its own page, or can book landing pages share one?
faq_plan.a: Give each book its own page, with one series page above them. Separate book landing pages let each title carry its own buy links and sample. The series page lists the books in reading order and links to each. Emergent builds both from a prompt, and you add the next book's page by asking for it.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between an author landing page and a page for one book?
faq_plan.a: An author landing page covers the writer and every book they have published, while a book page sells one title. The author page carries a bio, the full book list, events, and a newsletter signup. An attorney who writes about estate planning may also want a law firm landing page for clients. Keep the book page about the book, and link the two.

faq_plan.q: What should sit above the fold on a landing page for a book?
faq_plan.a: Put the cover, the title, a one-line hook, and the main button above the fold. For a book that has not launched, add the release date there too. On a landing page for a book, everything else, including reviews and the author bio, can sit below.

faq_plan.q: Which retailer links belong on a book landing page?
faq_plan.a: Link to every store that sells each format, not to one retailer. Ask your readers where they buy, and list those stores first. If a link pays you a commission, Google asks sites in affiliate programs to mark it rel=sponsored, whether the link was added by hand or generated by code.

faq_plan.q: How do I add a virtual launch event to a book landing page?
faq_plan.a: Add an event section with the date, the start time in your time zone, and a registration form. A virtual launch works like a webinar landing page: one registration form, then a reminder email with the link to join. On a page built with Emergent, registrations land in a database you own, and reminders go out through the email tool you connect.

plan.angle: The top 10 is galleries (Pinterest, Land-book, Landingfolio, Dribbble, ThemeForest), one email-platform guide (Kit) and builder example roundups (ConvertFlow, Unbounce). They show what a book page looks like and stop at the cover. This page defines the book landing page for searchers who want examples, then shows four working formats with what happens behind each button: a pre-order page that reads bonus receipts, a free-chapter page that grows a mailing list, a launch page that counts clicks by format, and an author page that sorts book club visit requests. The FAQ covers sections, retailer links, rel=sponsored on affiliate buy links and series pages.
